title: Cap. IX Arg. 3 Sol: Matt. 11:25; 13:11; Rom. 9:18 — antecedent good pleasure where the word was preached; efficacious grace prepared for some only
pass_a_gloss: Hither look those words of the Savior, Matt. xi. 25. I ascribe glory unto thee, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, that thou hast hidden these things from the wise and intelligent, and hast uncovered them unto babes. Even so, Father, because it so pleased thee. And those, Matt. xiii. 11. Unto you it is given to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven; unto them it is not given. Finally also that of the Apostle, often inculcated and to be inculcated unto all adversaries of special grace, Of whom he will he has mercy, and whom he will he hardens, Rom. ix. 18. All these places regard those unto whom the word of God was preached; and yet in all these is hinted the antecedent good pleasure of God, according to which efficacious grace was prepared for some, for others was not prepared.
pass_b_english: Here belong the Savior's words, Matt. 11:25: I give you glory, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, that you have hidden these things from the wise and understanding and uncovered them to infants. Yes, Father, for so it pleased you. And Matt. 13:11: To you it is given to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven; to them it is not given. And that saying of the Apostle, often pressed against every foe of special grace: He has mercy on whom he will, and whom he will he hardens (Rom. 9:18). All these texts concern those to whom God's word was preached — and yet in all of them God's antecedent good pleasure is hinted: efficacious grace prepared for some, not prepared for others.
source_text: Huc spectant illa Servatoris verba, Matth. xi. 25. Gloriam tibi tribuo Pater Domine caeli ac terrae, quod absconderis haec a sapientibus et intelligentibus, et ea detexeris infantibus. Etiam, Pater, quia ita placuit tibi. Et illa, Matth. xiii. 11. Vobis datum est nosse mysteria regni caelorum; illis non est datum. Denique et illud Apostoli, saepe inculcatum ac inculcandum omnibus specialis gratiae adversariis, Cujus vult miseretur, quem autem vult indurat, Rom. ix. 18. Omnia haec loca illos respiciunt quibus Dei verbum fuit praedicatum; et tamen in hisce omnibus innuatur antecedaneum Dei beneplacitum, secundum quod efficax gratia quibusdam praeparata fuit, aliis non fuit praeparata.
